blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Backed Assets retains transfer-agent freeze and burn authority over bIB01 balances under its Swiss DLT Act framework and operates KYC-gated primary issuance.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: bIB01 remains independently issuer-native and mintable on all seven authored token deployments; those native issuance rows stay canonical and outside Bridge Risk's bridge-control inventory. A separate six-chain BackedCCIPReceiver rail uses custody lock/release and Chainlink CCIP messaging against the native token addresses, with receiver owners, proxy upgrades, shared custody, router configuration, allowlists, and external message validation scored here. The receiver source contains no bIB01 mint or burn path, and BSC has no current receiver deployment.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex mint-bridge-boundary migration; bib01-backed verified finding

controls.capDescription: The receiver owner Safe administers the six-chain custody and CCIP route configuration; these powers govern transfer-rail machinery and do not replace any native issuer minter.
controls.evidence: At the 2026-08-16 observations, owner() returned 0x49754062e35f7591b93cc4f9915965be89643a65 on Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Gnosis, and Avalanche. The receiver was unpaused and registered bIB01 as token id 8492551 REGULAR on all five routes. controls.label: BackedCCIPReceiver transparent-proxy upgrade admin

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: At Ethereum block 25771145, Base 50068162, Polygon 92147098, Arbitrum 495307116, Gnosis 47762958, and Avalanche 92985493, each BackedCCIPReceiver proxy resolved to implementation 0x5ba339b721d32e603992bd96833d49283b6862dd and proxy-admin slot 0xd9c02791e7cf5d02d006556ceae76728920f3b0f. This separate transparent-proxy admin can replace receiver custody, allowlist, pause, and transfer-rail logic; it does not create a bIB01 mint or burn path.

controls.capDescription: The common receiver proxy-admin path can replace the six-chain CCIP receiver implementation and thereby change transfer-rail constraints without changing the seven native issuer controls.
controls.evidence: The same transparent BackedCCIPReceiver proxy address is live on Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Gnosis, and Avalanche. Current EIP-1967 reads on 2026-08-16 show implementation 0x5ba339b721d32e603992bd96833d49283b6862dd and proxy-admin 0xd9c02791e7cf5d02d006556ceae76728920f3b0f on all six routes. The receiver source contains custody lock/release and external messaging, not bIB01 mint or burn.

controls.label: BackedCCIPReceiver shared custody wallet

routeChecks.lockboxOrEscrow: custodyWallet() returned the same EOA 0x5f7a4c11bde4f218f0025ef444c369d838ffa2ad on all six receiver routes. The verified source transfers source bIB01 into this wallet and transfers the equivalent native token out on the destination receive path.
routeChecks.onchainAmountBounds: The custody address had zero deployed bytecode on all six current EVM reads, so it is a common EOA custody and failure domain rather than an independently inspected escrow contract.

controls.capDescription: The common custody EOA is the lock/release asset-holder for the six-chain CCIP receiver rail; its custody and withdrawal failure domain is bridge risk, not native issuance authority.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25771145, Base 50068162, Polygon 92147098, Arbitrum 495307116, Gnosis 47762958, and Avalanche 92985493, custodyWallet() returned the same 0x5f7a4c11bde4f218f0025ef444c369d838ffa2ad and the address had zero bytecode on every chain. This common EOA is retained as a shared custody failure domain; no bIB01 mint or burn is attributed to it.
